done.player_sees: Crew no longer hold two tickets that overlap. A ticket now needs 1:15 from landing to the next check-in. When a trip ends somewhere else, the crew fly straight from where they are to where they need to be. Before, a ticket home could land after the next ticket out had already left. Both triage dumps now show 0 crew-overlap errors.

A set's shared ticket out no longer moves 3 days earlier for one pilot's re-plan if that breaks someone else's 168 h rule or standby rest. The person being re-planned gets a ticket of their own instead. The seed 11 repro now gives 0 errors and 0 warnings.

A duty that ends 2 minutes late no longer costs the whole crew of the next trip. Crew short only of rest before their airline ticket out move to the next scheduled departure, and the first leg waits for them (at most 3 h). V7892 now flies with its own crew, 1h40 late, instead of being cancelled for $30K. New tickets out also keep a 30-minute rest margin when a departure allows.

Nothing changes in the game; this is test tooling. The invariant checker now judges commander's discretion at the last take-off (ORO.FTL.205(f)), so the legal 2:03 in seed 23 is no longer reported. It also checks factored invoices, and the test kit settles after each player step. The route unearned-cash check was already there.
A far-base reserve kept on standby at the station now gets their recovery rest recorded. The seed 7 Malta stat drops from 361 h to 168 h.

A burst of 'goes home early' messages in the same minute becomes one Inbox note per set, for example 'Set 2 at RUH: 7 crew go home early', with the names listed. Reasons read in plain words ('Over 100 block hours in 28 days', 'Short of rest (9:58 of 10:00)') on the note, the seat and the ticket. Day lists read 'Thu 9, Fri 10 and Sat 11 Sep 2027'.
An old save now loads fully the first time. Days off and standby are planned on the first load, not only after a save and reload. All 34 fixture saves come out identical after one load or two.

The 'On station' strip shows each set's real home date, for example 'Set 3 at London … home 10 Aug' instead of 1 Aug. Tickets from an earlier trip or from covering another set no longer count. The day count starts when the set arrives.

A crew member who is out of hours only because of past standby days is now taken off that one duty, and another set at the station flies it. VJ723 no longer carries a red out-of-hours alarm for 47 h until the gate. On the VNO seed 11 run, red alarms fell to 18 (0 out of hours) from the hunter's 23 (2 out of hours); my run was longer and was not done with exactly the same settings.

The crew-shortage card now says '(12:35, too close to the 13:00 limit)' instead of something that looks like a breach. Someone busy on a base tour is shown as 'busy on the Nantes tour until 2 Oct 2027' instead of one flight number.

done.player_sees: The study, the business case and the planner's ideas now use the player's own aircraft type in the cabin those aircraft really have. A new A320 airline with all-economy jets gets an A320 all-economy case, not an A321neo with business seats. If the player picks a type they don't own, or business seats their aircraft lack, the case shows a warning just under the verdict.

The case, the ideas and the ACMI comparison now charge the same aircraft cost per block hour that the route P&L will. That is the average over the player's own aircraft of the type: an owned jet costs only its insurance, a leased one its rent too. List rent is used only when they own none of that type. Cases on owned jets are no longer far too gloomy, so the 'case -38K vs actual +295K' kind of gap shrinks.

The demand a study is measured against is fixed on the day the study is done. A reopened case, the Sales tab cabin quote and the analyst's advice now read the same market weeks later, instead of 373 becoming 1,022. Older saves fix this value once when they load.

The monthly route P&L charges each aircraft for its own hours. An owned jet and a leased one covering a C-check in the same month are each charged at their own rate, so one month no longer jumps to $111K of aircraft time.

When passengers are denied boarding there is now a route note, for example 'MTL351: 11 passengers denied boarding'. It names the aircraft and its seats, how many volunteers took a voucher, and the EU261 paid. When a C-check cover is close to departure and the stand-in jet is smaller than the bookings, a right-size sub-charter is tried first.

Suspend now offers 'Fly next 9, refund rest · $X' or 'Refund all · $Y'. Rows show Ticket money back, Cost to us and Money out. Wind down says 'The next N rotations fly; later ones are refunded' instead of 'no refunds'. Plurals are fixed ('1 rotation ... comes off', '1 flies / is sub-chartered / waits'), and the text now says 'An A320 on ACMI' instead of 'A A320'.

The study's off-peak and peak loads now follow the market's own season (a winter-sun route peaks in winter) and use the loads of an established route, past the launch ramp. The aircraft sentence comes from how many travellers are turned away at peak, so it no longer contradicts the loads. Where payload caps the seats well below the cabin, it says so, e.g. 'An A320 can sell only 142 seats here (payload)'.

The rival that cuts fares at launch is named. When there is no nonstop rival, the one-stop carrier is named by its hub, e.g. 'Turkish Airlines cut its fares via Istanbul 15 % for 4 months'. The 'launch campaign done' note now gives the awareness reached instead of repeating the fare cut. The route's Sales tab shows the rival cut and its end date.
A route with no flown month shows a muted dash in the Network list, in the 'Last 3 months' tile and in the route page's Result KPI. There is no red and no falling arrow.
The airport search in the route builder and in the position/A-check search finds cities typed without accents: Sao Paulo, Malaga, Krakow, Tromso and Istanbul.
The business case steps through the calendar months from the first flight, with the first and last months pro-rated. A 7-month seasonal route now counts 7 flying months, not 8.

Pressing Go now saves the case's likely year month by month. The route page's 'Result by month' chart shows the plan as dashed outline bars behind the actual bars. A 'vs plan' line (e.g. '-$126K, 4 months: +$3.1K against +$129K') has a '?' that explains it. If the launch pushes the first flight later, the plan moves with it. Old routes show nothing extra.

A study ordered from a planner idea carries that idea's aircraft into the case draft. The verdict adds 'The planner guessed a 12 % margin once the route is known; the study's first year says X %.' The map's route card shows the next flight in local times, e.g. 'Fri 2 Jul 2027 10:00 MLA → 13:35 ESB'.

A client never has two live leads for the same kind of work, and a visit no longer opens a second tender in the same round. Meetings are on working days (Sun-Thu in the Gulf). No beach series to Burgas in November or to Rhodes or Olbia in winter. Summer-only resorts get a series only between May and October, and a leisure airline's winter base flies to resorts that are open in winter.

Federations (FPF, DFB, RFU...) fly one national-team away game at a time to a foreign capital: 'Qualifier in', 'Nations League away in', 'Friendly in'. Rugby unions fly to the Six Nations grounds. Club league away days only go to cities with a top-flight club.

'Half-term charters' only for a short British programme starting in February, the last week of May or October. 'Summer peak' and 'Holiday peak cover' only for June-August starts. British July and August series can be called 'School holidays to X'.

The cold-lead Inbox message reads as normal prose, with no 'Yes: $982K...'. Names ending in s get the right possessive: "Rainbow Tours' lead". The same fix covers the strike notice and the visit offer text.

Frontex no longer asks for relief flights. European ministries never rotate troops to AUSSOM. A lost offer is never lost to the client's own rival company or to a rival that has ceased trading. LV/BG home missions were not added; see notes.

The offer dialog's aircraft row labels its number 'margin'. The open row and the analyst card add 'Profit after lease and crew about $X', and a '?' explains what the margin leaves out. On the Jeddah offer: analyst margin about 76 %, profit after lease and crew about $773K.

On a phone held sideways, the title sits beside the tabs and the standing and outlook tiles are one short chip row.

Governments in low-risk countries (EU/EEA, UK, CH, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, KR, SG, AE, QA) pay 85% of invoices on time, the rest 0-15 days late; other governments still pay 25-90 days late. done.player_sees: An aircraft that ends a job at an outstation a month before a paint shop or check away from base now flies home first, then on to the shop later. In the repro, LZ-UFQ goes WAW to SOF on 10 Mar instead of sitting at Warsaw until 11 Apr. Its A-check then happens at Sofia for $25K instead of $30K, and it picks up another contract. The fix is in contracts/schedule.ts: planPositioning(viaHome) for ferries to a shop, and the relink gap planner allows the home hop before a maintenance stop away from base. The out-and-back hop around checks at home is still barred.
Only one world event can be live per zone. The Iraq war and the Iraq airspace closure no longer overlap, so there is no 'reopened' message while the airspace is still shut.

Weather events follow real seasons: the Punta Cana hurricane only June to November, the Sindh floods July to September, calima and Madeira wind only in the winter half. Each event has a cooldown by kind: disasters 540 days, coups, wars, unrest and airspace 180, strikes 60, ash 30, airline failures 5 years, the rival failure 60. A repeat within 120 days reads 'again', for example 'Italian air traffic controllers strike again (ENAV)'. Older saves rebuild the last start of each event from the events they kept; a new game is unchanged.

An automatic A-check that needs a ferry home from an outstation now leaves time for a crew to fly out on the airline and rest first. The flat 9-hour lead is gone. In the repro, 9H-XBG at Terceira is booked for 18 Dec 17:15 with its ferry the next day at 11:40, crewed. Before, the check was booked for the same day, the crew shortage alarm fired and the check slipped a day.

Crew tickets no longer invent nonstops to Greenland: Malta to Kangerlussuaq is FR to Copenhagen, then Air Greenland (GL) from Copenhagen. Heathrow to Kangerlussuaq goes the same way through Copenhagen, and Lisbon to Nuuk goes through Reykjavik on GL. Air Greenland is added with CPH-SFJ, CPH-GOH and KEF-GOH. Royal Air Maroc keeps to its real long-haul routes (JFK, IAD, MIA, BOS, YUL, GRU, DOH) plus Europe, Africa and the Middle East within 6,000 km, so no Santiago or Los Angeles. Side effect: Goma tickets now connect at Luanda.

The low-cash, below-zero and credit-headroom cards now say 'Still to come from invoices $X'. A sold invoice counts only the part the bank has not already advanced. The 'sell one to the bank' hint only appears when an unsold invoice exists. On Finance, the cash trend reads 'up $664K since 1 Jun 2027' instead of 'in 3 months'.

Between two trips from the same outstation, a new plan only flies the aircraft home and back when that costs less than waiting there. The comparison is fuel, fees and maintenance for the hop against parking plus the crew's airline tickets home and back. Waits longer than 8 days still go home. Hops already planned in a save are kept. Tapping a 2 to 8 day idle stretch at such an outstation shows 'Waits at Helsinki (cheaper than a ferry home).'

done.player_sees: When a leg is handed to a rival during a disruption (AOG, stranded, far-stranded or sick-crew cards), it no longer leaves on time as if the rival were already there. The leg now leaves no earlier than now + 6 h, or later if the rival needs longer to fly in from its base, and the legs after it keep a turn between them. The option chips say 'First leg ~9h 40m late' and so does the result line. The delay counts against us (a late flight under our flight number, with the contract's late rule on arrival). In the repro save, XY967 GOI now leaves about 9.7 h late, flown by Avion Express from Vilnius.

The medical, diversion and bird-strike cards name the crew on board, e.g. 'Purser Rita Teixeira called for a doctor on board; Captain Stephanie Abela is talking to MedLink, the doctors on the ground.' After a medical diversion one quiet inbox line closes the story: 'The passenger was taken to hospital in Bucharest. The crew filed their report.'
In Fleet > Hangar > Side, the floor bands sit under the wheels and stay inside the card. They are measured again once the aircraft art has loaded or a row reflows. Checked on Mac, iPad and iPhone.

A new in-flight card, 'XY123: disruptive passenger', with the purser and captain named. The choices are 'Continue; police meet the aircraft' (a report goes to the home base's authority, at no cost) or 'Divert and offload at <city>'. Diverting adds about an hour on the ground and the delay is not counted against us. We pay a police call-out, plus handling and fuel on a charter, and half of it shows as a receivable from 'Passenger' due in 90 days. The Company safety line counts disruptive passengers and the diversion map shows the card. It is rare (about 3 in 10,000 legs, scaled by how busy the current stretch of play is), in its own band after the other in-flight events. If there is nowhere to divert to, the player gets a warning instead of a card.

Each AOG fault now has its own repair time and cost: a tyre is 3–8 h for $3–8K, brakes 4–12 h, a windshield 10–30 h for $25–45K, IDG 10–30 h, fan blade damage 24–72 h, and tug damage 24–96 h for $50–150K. A big airport takes some of the outstation wait off. APU and bleed faults are no longer AOGs: they show as gate delays such as 'Technical: APU inoperative (MEL), ground power needed'.

Weather diversions fit the season and the place: snow only from November to March at 40 degrees latitude or more (the southern hemisphere flipped), fog in autumn and winter, thunderstorms in the warm months or all year in the tropics. No more snow at Riga in September or at Tenerife in July. The map weather marks use the same list.

Client change requests give a reason that fits the client, e.g. 'their hotel transfers run late' (tour operator), 'their own inbound flight is late' (airline), 'the match moved to an evening kick-off' (sports), 'their board meeting runs over' (corporate). A medical (or disruptive-passenger) event with no airport near enough to divert to no longer pauses the game on a card with one option: a warning appears in the inbox and the flight carries on.

No more '..' at the end of result lines, '1 day' instead of '1 days' on the sick-crew card, and possessives such as 'moved at Jet2's request' or 'at Thomas' request'. Prague, Sofia and Tallinn bases name their authority (the UCL, the DG CAA, the Transport Administration); Morocco's DGAC is added too.

Finance at a glance: 'Office & sales' is now olive and 'Bank & interest' plum, so there are no longer two greens or two oranges. The proposed colours #8fb339 and #8d86a8 failed the dataviz validator (lightness band, chroma, colour-blind check), so validated ones are used: dark #6d6a00 and #9e36bb, light #5f7300 and #91006f. On the iPhone and iPad home-screen app, the light look gets a status bar with dark text and the dark look a black one. A '?' next to Settings > Appearance explains that this applies the next time the app opens.

Gate delays fit the season and the place: 'Weather: de-icing, queue at the pad' and 'Weather: snow clearance' from November to March at 45 degrees N or more, and 'Weather: thunderstorms on the route' from June to August. Everyday reasons are added: 'Late passengers: one missing, bags offloaded', 'Wheelchair assistance late', 'Catering short-loaded', and 'Refused boarding: a drunk passenger, bags offloaded' (the gate version of the disruptive passenger). Weather, missing-passenger and refused-boarding delays are not counted against us. The crew name pools for Malta, Italy, Romania, Poland, Britain, France, Slovakia and Cape Verde grow to about 20 real names each.

In Hangar > From above, each aircraft is drawn in its livery: fuselage colour, tail colour on the rear 12 %, engine cowls in the cowl colour. Plain airframes stay white with grey cowls. On the Schedule, the date of the first day on screen stays at the left edge of the timeline while that day is on screen.
